notes: Summary: Helix builds an in-IDE copilot for enterprise customers (VS Code + Web IDE). High priority: reproducible code completions across releases and low variance in streaming behavior.
Key ask from CTO (Nalin Rao): 'If we ship a model update we need to guarantee repeatable completions for our unit test prompts and a rollback path with feature flags.'
Evaluation priority order: 1) model/version pinning + canaries, 2) deterministic replay / eval gates, 3) telemetry + retention controls, 4) cost guardrails for heavy autocompletion workloads.

Latency targets: first-token < 60ms on warm sessions; streaming token cadence <= 25ms for in-editor feel. Throughput: support 1k concurrent completion sessions per zone with predictable tail latencies.
Sensitivity: cannot ingest full customer repos for hosted training; prefer client-side prefix caching and per-customer KV cache. Data residency not strict but telemetry must be scrubbed.
Model preferences: open weights preferred (Llama variants), but willing to run Redwood-managed proprietary variants if pinning and reproducibility guarantees exist.
Quote from lead PM (Elena): 'We need rollback semantics that don't change behavior for active sessions — ephemeral fallback ok, but pinned requests must remain deterministic.'
Notes on rollout model: want canary % by user cohort, AB test on completion correctness (safety + build breakage), automatic eval gate that checks testset regressions before wider traffic shift.
Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to pay for dedicated pools if latency and determinism are met. Looking for Optimize suggestions: batching thresholds that preserve streaming cadence.
Security/compliance: SSO + SAML for company users, audit logs for admin actions, KMS integration for keys, retention controls for prompts and completions (90/180/365 options discussed).
